messages:
Fiona (Design): Quick notes from today's catalog crit. Focus areas: 1) presets discoverability — thinking about a compact 'saved views' pill row with keyboard arrow nav, 2) performance badges are visually loud and causing horizontal jank in compare, 3) pin semantics confusing (single vs bulk pin), 4) some low-contrast badge text and missing aria context. Thoughts?

Owen (PM): Saved views pill row sounds promising. Also a product ask: customers want to pin an entire selection (bulk-pin) so they can preserve a set of model versions for later audits. We should discuss scope: user vs workspace.

Rajat (Eng): Bulk-pin adds complexity but doable. We can store pinned_collections { user_id, name, entries:[{model_id,version}], created_at }. For MVP: user-scoped collections, editable in settings. Edge-case: if a model retires, mark entry stale.

Bea (Frontend): Badge problem: current badges are full-bleed pills with shadows that push columns. Proposal: 1) switch to inline ghost chips (no heavy bg), 2) constrain to max-width and ellipsize, 3) right-align and give names a fixed min-width to avoid wrap. CSS idea: `.perf-chip{ background:transparent; border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.06); color:var(--muted); font-size:11px; padding:2px 6px; border-radius:6px; max-width:80px; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; }`

Tess (A11y): Accessibility checklist: chips must be focusable and announce context (e.g. `aria-label=\"98th percentile latency: 220 milliseconds\"`). Saved-views pill row should be a horizontal toolbar with roving tabindex and arrow-key nav. Bulk-pin UI must expose scope and allow keyboard selection of multiple rows (shift+arrow or checkbox). Color contrast: ensure chip text >= 4.5:1 for interactive elements or bump to 14px semi-bold if lower.

Fiona (Design): UX flows: small pill row above filters with left/right arrows for overflow and a "+" to save current filters as a view. For bulk-pin, propose a small multi-select mode in compare: checkboxes appear, mini toolbar shows "Pin selection" -> opens small modal to name collection. Modal microcopy: "Save selection as a pinned collection — visible only to you".

Owen (PM): Agree on microcopy. For MVP collections are user-only. Track analytics: `bulk_pin.created` with count, `pin.collection_applied`, include model_ids list hash to avoid huge payloads. We'll evaluate workspace-sharing later.

Rajat (Eng): Implementation notes: 1) API endpoints: POST /v1/pin_collections, GET /v1/pin_collections?user=me, DELETE /v1/pin_collections/:id. 2) Migration: continue storing single pinned_version as before, map to a default single-item collection. 3) Performance: avoid loading full collection details in the compare list; only fetch IDs and lazy-load metadata.

ops-bot: ops-bot: feature branch `feat/catalog-bulk-pin-views` built and pushed to staging: https://staging.redwood.ai/catalog/compare

Bea (Frontend): Checklist before PR: 1) pill-row UI with roving tabindex + tooltip, 2) ghost-style perf chips and right-align, 3) multi-select keyboard support (shift+click and space to toggle), 4) bulk-pin modal with accessible form, 5) aria-labels for all chips and pin buttons. I'll include screenshots and keyboard flow in PR description.

Tess (A11y): I'll test NVDA/VoiceOver and keyboard-only flows on staging. Also review announcements: when applying a saved view say "Applied view: <name>" and for bulk-pin success use polite live region: "Pinned 6 versions to collection \"Q2-benchmark\"".

Fiona (Design): Small microcopy set: pill row label "Saved views"; pill action "Apply view"; pill tooltip "Apply saved filters to this page"; bulk-pin modal title "Save pinned collection"; modal help text "Collections are saved to your account and can be applied to future compares." Toast on retired entry: "Some pinned versions are retired and marked unavailable."

Owen (PM): I'll create the ticket with acceptance criteria: pill row visible & keyboardable, perf chips restyled and do not cause horizontal layout shift, bulk-pin modal + API, analytics events, accessibility checks. Target: stage deploy next Friday.

Rajat (Eng): One UX edge-case: when applying a collection to a compare that includes models not currently loaded, we should surface a non-blocking banner: "Collection applied; 2 entries not in this compare." Do not auto-select.

Bea (Frontend): :+1: I'll wire the partial-apply banner and include a CTA to "Open model list" which shows missing entries.

Tess (A11y): :+1: Also ensure banners are focusable and announced.

Fiona (Design): Thanks team. I'll update the figma with the pill-row and modal screens and drop links in the ticket. :sparkles:
